title: Show and clear the DNF package cache on Fedora to free disk space
summary: On Fedora, DNF keeps downloaded package files and package lists in a cache folder, and it can grow to a hundred megabytes or more. This shows how big that cache is and then empties it to free disk space. Installed programs are not touched.

aliases.text: how big is dnf cache fedora
clean dnf cache to free space
освободить место на диске fedora dnf
почистить кэш dnf чтобы освободить место

steps.explain: Check how much space the DNF cache uses. This only reads the folder and changes nothing. Look at the first value: it is the size, for example 102M means about 102 megabytes.
Delete all cached package files and repository metadata. Installed programs stay as they are. DNF downloads the cache again when it needs it.
steps.expect: Ends with a line like: Removed 18 files, 9 directories (total of 102 MiB). 0 errors occurred.

rollback.explain: Nothing needs to be undone. The cache comes back on its own the next time you run a dnf command, such as dnf install or dnf upgrade, and it needs an internet connection.

warnings: Only the downloaded cache is deleted. Installed programs and your personal files are not changed.
The next dnf install or upgrade has to download the package lists again, so it is slower and needs an internet connection.
